title: Indefinite Integration
summary: This unit introduced integration as the inverse process of differentiation, defining it both as a method for finding antiderivatives and as a tool for calculating the area under a curve. It establishes essential terminology, such as the integrand, the constant of integration (C), and the distinction between indefinite and definite integrals, while providing a library of standard integrals for particular functions, such as polynomial, trigonometric, and exponential

13.3 Integration of some Particular Functions

  • 8 Indefinite Integration Note: Constant of integration c is added everywhere, so in future we will not write ‘where c is constant of integration’.

13.4 Integration by Substitution

  • In section 13.3, we have taken into consideration the integrations for which a formula can directly be used.
  • But sometimes integrand cannot be directly integrated using standard formula.
  • In order to convert it into a form for which standard formula can be applied, we substitute some function in place of some other function and this technique of obtaining the integration is known as integration by substitution method.
  • Using appropriate formula we can obtain the integral of given integrand in terms of t.
